chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from al-Nakha'i from Ibn Abi Umayr from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who forgot to throw the pebbles at the Jamarat. He said, 'He returns and throws them.' I said, 'And if he forgot them until he arrived in Mecca?' He said, 'He returns and throws them separately, placing an hour between each two throws.' I said, 'And if he forgot or was unaware until the time passed and he departed?' He said, 'He is not obliged to repeat them.'

His saying (peace be upon him) 'He is not obliged to repeat them' means he is not obliged to repeat them in this year, although it is obligatory for him to repeat it in the following year, either by himself if he is able, or by ordering someone to act on his behalf. And this is because the days of throwing are the days of Tashriq; so if they pass for him, nothing is obligatory upon him except in the coming year during similar days.

key_terms.أَيَّامُ التَّشْرِيقِ: The days of Tashriq (11th, 12th, and 13th of Dhu al-Hijjah)
key_terms.بِسَاعَةٍ: For an hour (the interval between each throw)
key_terms.رَمْيَ الْجِمَارِ: Throwing pebbles at the Jamarat (pillars) during Hajj
key_terms.مُتَفَرِّقاً: Separately (referring to throwing the pebbles individually rather than together)
key_terms.يَنُوبُ عَنْهُ: Acting as a proxy/representative on his behalf

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a pilgrim who forgets to throw the Jamarat pebbles until after leaving Mecca?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the distinction between forgetting the Jamarat throws while still in Mina versus after departing for Mea, establishing that missing the specific days of Tashriq exempts one from immediate repetition. The ruling emphasizes the temporal nature of this pillar, allowing for deferred fulfillment in the subsequent year either personally or via proxy, reflecting the Shia juristic principle of ease in ritual obligations when circumstances prevent timely performance.
